elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Operative §12.3 states that Customer has made no non-compete commitment, and revised §12.4 affirmatively permits Customer to develop, market, sell, or acquire any competing product or service.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Operative §12.3 permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory and to develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no restriction at all; instead, §§12.3 and 12.4 permit activity involving any product or service. The condition requiring a restriction to be narrowly limited is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the term.
elements.evidence: No restriction applies during or after the term. The original 24-month post-term restriction has been removed and replaced with affirmative permission.

elements.element: Any restriction has a maximum duration of 12 months.
elements.evidence: There is no operative restriction or restricted period, so no restriction exceeds the 12-month cap.

elements.element: Internal development is carved out from any restriction.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 expressly permit Customer to develop any product or service, including one that competes with Vendor.

elements.element: Acquisitions are carved out from any restriction.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 expressly permit Customer to acquire any product or service, including one that competes with Vendor.

result.reason: The redline completely removes the non-compete and confirms that Customer may operate in any field or territory. It therefore satisfies the preferred position and, independently, all fallback limitations because no narrower restriction remains. The change is confined to eliminating the conflicting restriction in §12.4 and introduces no unrelated obligation or contradiction.
